source_title: Oil prices cross $115 per barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke supply fears
source_excerpt: Crude oil prices continued their upward march on Friday, with Brent crossing $115 a barrel as attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf heightened fears of supply disruptions. The benchmarks were also heading for their fourth consecutive monthly rise, with US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April.Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75 per cent, to $115.74 a barrel by 0122 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 72 cents, or 0.71 per cent, to $102.72.Brent was on course for a nearly 14 per cent gain in October, while WTI was set to jump around 15 per cent.
